To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we have found that the data from CDF on τ + τ -+ 2 jets final state can be used to derive stringent limits on Higgs boson mass in the MSSM; (ii) these limits are stronger than those obtained using other channels; and (iii) they are competitive with the limits obtained by LEP2 and the Tevatron.

the CDF data on τ + +2jets final states can be used to set limits on the masses of the neutral Higgs bosons of the MSSM, and that the data can also be used to set stringent limits on the masses and couplings of third generation lepto-quarks.
the CDF bbτ + τ− search can be used to set bounds on the Higgs masses of the Minimal Supersymetric Model (MSS) for tanβ =50.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for new physics at high energy colliders, in particular the Tevatron and LEP.
the search for supersymmetric Higgs particles in the context of the Minimal Supersymmetic Standard Model (MssM) at the CDF and D0 experiments at the Tevatron.
the phenomenology of the Minimal Supersymetric Standard Model (Mssm) with a non-universal Higgs mass matrix (NUHM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no MSSM Higgs bosons with masses up to 200 GeV are allowed if tanβ is larger than 50.
, if the MSSM is correct and tanβ>50, then the Higgs sector is already excluded.
, for the MSSM, the Tevatron data exclude the range 150 GeV < m A < 190 GeV for tanβ = 50, while for 30 < tanβ < 60 the excluded range is 140 GeV < m H 0 < 200 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Tevatron is now able to constrain the Higgs sector in a very similar way to what the LEP experiments have done for the SM Higgs boson.
the existing Tevatron Run II data is already constraining the Higgs boson mass in the MSSM up to tanβ ∼ 50.
the Tevatron data on τ +τ − + 2 jet events can provide a powerful tool for constraining the Higgs sector of the MSSM, especially for large values of tanβ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in the absence of a direct observation, the Tevatron can be used to place very stringent limits on the Higgs sector of the MSSM, as well as other models with an extended Higgs sector.
the τ + τ − final state can be used to place strong constraints on models with extended scalar sectors, including the MSSM, even when the Higgs boson decays to τ + τ − are kinematically forbidden.
the Tevatron is a powerful discovery machine for supersymmetric Higgs particles.
